chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ali ibn Ahmad from Musa ibn Umar from Muhammad ibn Mansur from him, who said:
I asked him about the shading for the Muhrim (one in Ihram), he said: He is not shaded except due to a defect or illness.

key_terms.لِلْمُحْرِمِ: For the one in Ihram (state of consecration)

ai.seo_question: When is a Muhrim allowed to be shaded during Hajj?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to clarify the specific conditions under which a Muhrim may seek shade, distinguishing between permissible shading due to a defect or illness and the general prohibition. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that the restriction on shading is lifted when it is necessary to alleviate physical hardship or prevent harm, thereby balancing ritual purity with bodily well-being.
